cards.name: Parabiosis
cards.flavor: Two mice, one bloodstream. Neither was consulted.
cards.notes: Pain Split (the user, 2026-10-17): target creature and the creature facing it share their Health out equally (the odd point to the one that had less). Not damage, not healing: nothing answers it.
cards.picture: Two hospital beds facing each other with a single blood bag hung between them, the tube running from a huge glowing-pink healthy creature to a grey wilted one, both ending up the same shade of medium pink.

cards.name: Peer Review
cards.flavor: Interesting results. Shame they don't replicate.
cards.notes: The user, 2026-10-17 (Peer Review kept for another archetype: a reveal plus an effect): reveal target enemy creature's slot, its plans and what hides there, and its findings are retracted: Blackout 2, its ability and effects switched off.
cards.picture: Three reviewers in lab coats with magnifying glasses peering at a scientist's poster, red RETRACTED stamps hammering onto it, the scientist's hidden second poster behind it dragged into the light.

cards.name: Geomagnetic Reversal
cards.flavor: North is south now. The compass apologises. The pigeons do not.
cards.notes: The user, 2026-10-16: target creature's Attack and Health trade places, on either side. Its Attack becomes its Health as it is now, and its Health its Attack: a glass cannon becomes a wall, a wall a glass cannon, and a creature with no Attack is left with no Health and dies.
cards.picture: A globe with its magnetic field lines flipping over, the N and S labels swapping places mid-air, a scientist staring at a compass whose needle spins wildly, and a flock of birds flying in confused loops.

cards.name: Research Lab
cards.flavor: Results in five years. Funding for two.
cards.notes: Utopia's research: send for a spell from your deck; it joins your next hand.
cards.picture: A gleaming laboratory with scientists in white coats pulling glowing cards out of test tubes and a centrifuge, a grant deadline clock ticking on the wall.

cards.name: Clone
cards.flavor: Twice the sheep. Half the soul.
cards.notes: When it enters, summon a random creature from your deck. Future: Clone (copies a friendly creature).
cards.picture: Dolly the sheep in a lab coat and goggles proudly presenting a row of identical sheep behind her.

cards.name: Hypermetamorphosis
cards.flavor: Caterpillar, cocoon, middle manager. Nature is healing.
cards.notes: +1/+1 for good each Dawn. Future: Evolution (each step unlocks an ability).
cards.picture: Left to right: a caterpillar, a cocoon, and a hatched office worker in a tie with butterfly wings, briefcase in hand, dead inside.

cards.name: Extremophile
cards.flavor: Survived five mass extinctions. Your opinion won't be the sixth.
cards.notes: Unbothered, and it heals 1 each Dusk.
cards.picture: A chubby tardigrade lounging in a pool of lava in sunglasses, a tiny cocktail in its claw.

cards.name: Philosophy PhD
cards.flavor: Eight years of Kant. Would you like fries with that?
cards.notes: A draw each Dawn; the student debt costs it 1 Health each Dusk.
cards.picture: A graduate in cap and gown flipping burgers at a fast-food grill, the diploma pinned up next to the menu.

cards.name: Mathematician
cards.flavor: Showed her work. Nobody checked it.
cards.notes: Each Dawn a random enemy creature gets -1 Attack for good.
cards.picture: The confused math lady meme: a woman squinting while equations, triangles and integrals float around her head.

cards.name: Quantum Physicist
cards.flavor: In two places at once. Late to both.
cards.notes: Swap. Whoever hits it is Exhausted: observing it collapses them.
cards.picture: A physicist split down the middle, one half of him see-through, holding two coffees and checking two watches.

cards.name: Perpetual Motion Machine
cards.flavor: Runs forever. The patent office stopped answering in 1911.
cards.notes: A draw each Dawn, and it heals 1 each Dusk.
cards.picture: A hamster running in a wheel that powers a fan, which blows on the hamster, which keeps running.

cards.name: Particle Accelerator
cards.flavor: Found the God particle. Lost the car keys.
cards.notes: Each Dawn, 2 damage to a random creature on either side (side effects).
cards.picture: A huge ring-shaped tunnel seen from above, a tiny scientist on a bicycle racing around it after a glowing dot.

cards.name: Genetically Modified Organism
cards.flavor: Organic. Gluten-free. Bench-presses 200.
cards.notes: +2/+2 for good when it enters; the side effects cost it 1 Health each Dusk.
cards.picture: A ripe tomato with huge bodybuilder arms, flexing, a NON-GMO sticker peeling off its skin.

cards.name: Surveillance Giraffe
cards.flavor: Heart the size of a TV. Still can't reach its own feet.
cards.notes: When it enters, Reveal a random enemy creature's slot: it sees over the fog.
cards.picture: A giraffe whose neck runs out of the top of the picture and comes back in from the top further along, its head hanging upside down, peeking.

cards.name: Pioneer
cards.flavor: First human on Mars. First eviction on Mars.
cards.notes: Leapfrog: it jumps over creatures to an empty slot.
cards.picture: An astronaut planting a flag on a red desert next to a sign: FOR RENT $9999.

cards.name: Placebo
cards.flavor: Clinically proven to work on people who believe it works.
cards.notes: +3 Health for good.
cards.picture: A sugar pill the size of a melon labelled MIRACLE on a spoonful of sugar, and a skinny man next to it flexing a non-existent bicep, very proud.

cards.name: Vaccine
cards.flavor: Side effects include not dying, and 5G.
cards.notes: Cleanses its statuses, all of them; side effect: -1 Attack for this Day (sore arm).
cards.picture: A syringe with a tiny Wi-Fi antenna on its plunger and full signal bars above it.

cards.name: Climate Change
cards.flavor: The scientists agreed. The weather didn't wait.
cards.notes: Every creature is Burned for 2 Days and gets Heat Signature 1.
cards.picture: A polar bear standing on a single ice cube floating in a cocktail glass, a paper umbrella beside it.

cards.name: Overpopulation
cards.flavor: Eight billion people and nobody to cover my shift.
cards.notes: Summon 2 random creatures from your deck.
cards.picture: A tiny Earth with people crammed all over it like a full elevator, one man balancing on top on one foot.

cards.name: Black Hole
cards.flavor: What goes in doesn't come out. Like your tax refund.
cards.notes: 4 damage to the creature and its neighbors; 2 damage to you (side effects). Future: Black Hole repositioning.
cards.picture: A swirling black hole sucking in a cow, a sofa, a single sock and a tax form.

cards.name: Stasis Field
cards.flavor: Frozen in time. Like your salary.
cards.notes: Shield 3 on target creature: for 3 Days, counting this one, it takes no combat damage. It goes with the creature (the user, 2026-10-16: a slot can't have a shield).
cards.picture: A man frozen mid-sneeze inside a giant block of green jelly, the droplets hanging in the air.

cards.name: Absolute Zero
cards.flavor: Minus 273. The office AC, as set by Gary.
cards.notes: Every creature is Exhausted.
cards.picture: A man frozen solid at his desk holding a frozen cup of coffee, the thermostat on the wall reading -273.

cards.name: Splitting The Atom
cards.flavor: Science's greatest achievement: a really big bang.
cards.notes: 6 damage to a random enemy creature; 2 damage to you (side effects).
cards.picture: A lumberjack in a flannel shirt splitting a glowing atom on a tree stump with an axe, a mushroom cloud rising behind him.

cards.name: Gene Editing
cards.flavor: Bigger, stronger, slightly radioactive.
cards.notes: +2/+2 for good; side effect: Burned for 2 Days. Future: gene editing as Persistent Stat Modifications.
cards.picture: A pair of scissors cutting a DNA double helix, a strip of tape sticking a unicorn horn onto it.

cards.name: Accelerationism
cards.flavor: Whatever the problem, more technology. Whatever the cost, faster.
cards.notes: Gamble, accelerationism's way: every outcome pays and every one costs (the user: drawbacks, 2026-10-16). Your creatures take 2 and get +3 Attack for good (on the brink, then boom); or progress for everyone, +2/+2 for good to every creature, the enemy's too; or Borrowed Time this Day, then 3 damage to each: on the brink they deal double, and any left at 0 are back to 1 at Dusk (the user's Borrowed Time, 2026-10-16).
cards.picture: A tech founder in a hoodie flooring the accelerator of a rocket-powered car toward a cliff edge, the road on fire behind him, a bridge of glowing circuit boards assembling itself in mid-air just ahead of the wheels.

cards.name: Cold Fusion
cards.flavor: Clean, limitless energy. Slight meltdown risk. Mostly fine.
cards.notes: On the Brink: at 2 Health or less it deals double. The reactor runs hot: 1 damage to itself each Dusk.
cards.picture: A tabletop fusion reactor glowing white-hot in a jar on a garage workbench, the warning gauge in the red, two engineers in sunglasses giving a thumbs-up.

cards.name: Antimatter
cards.flavor: One gram costs 62 trillion dollars. Worth it.
cards.notes: On the Brink: at 2 Health or less it deals double. When ready, 2 damage to itself: it starts on the brink.
cards.picture: A tiny shimmering particle in a magnetic bottle, its mirror image annihilating the lab bench around it, a physicist ducking behind a clipboard.

cards.name: Biohacking
cards.flavor: Ten thousand volts and a nootropic smoothie.
cards.notes: Target friendly creature takes 3 damage, then gets +4 Attack for good. Too weak for it, it dies trying.
cards.picture: A shirtless tech bro in a garage strapped to car batteries, LED implants glowing under his skin, a smoothie in one hand and a soldering iron in the other.

cards.name: Blood Transfusion
cards.flavor: Young blood, old money.
cards.notes: Heal target friendly creature 6: back from the brink, just in time.
cards.picture: An old billionaire in a recliner hooked up to an IV bag labelled TEEN, reading the stock prices, his skin looking twenty years younger.

cards.name: Evolution Theory
cards.flavor: Only the fittest survive. We've been making ours fitter.
cards.notes: Trend for 3 Days, Survival of the Fittest: each Dusk the creature with the least Health on the board, either side, takes 3. Utopia's creatures are the ones that grow.
cards.picture: Darwin in a lab coat at a chalkboard, the classic march of progress drawn on it from ape to man to a huge muscled lab-grown superman, and a tiny weak creature at the start of the line being crossed out.

cards.name: Mutation
cards.flavor: Three extra arms. One fewer kidney.
cards.notes: +3 Attack for good on target friendly creature; side effect: it loses 1 Health for good.
cards.picture: A lab rat in a cage flexing three muscular arms, a scientist taking notes and quietly sliding a fourth arm onto the clipboard.

cards.name: Exponential Growth
cards.flavor: It doubles every day. That's what worries us.
cards.notes: +1/+1 for good on each of your creatures; side effect: they're Burned for 2 Days.
cards.picture: A petri dish overflowing onto the lab bench, the colony spilling over the edge and climbing up the wall, a scientist backing away holding the lid.

cards.name: Scientific Method
cards.flavor: Hypothesis, experiment, grant renewal.
cards.notes: Each Dawn, +1 Attack for good on a random friendly creature (peer reviewed).
cards.picture: A scientist in goggles carefully pouring a glowing liquid into a beaker on a bench crowded with labelled flasks, a whiteboard behind her reading HYPOTHESIS → EXPERIMENT → GRANT.

cards.name: Frankenstein
cards.flavor: It's alive! It's ALIVE! It's suing.
cards.notes: An abomination that grows: +1/+1 for good each Dawn. Side effect: it arrives Burned for 2 Days (the lightning).
cards.picture: A towering stitched-together monster sitting up on a lab table under a lightning bolt, bolts in its neck smoking, the mad scientist cheering with both arms up.

cards.name: Chimera
cards.flavor: Lion, goat, snake. The ethics committee was on holiday.
cards.notes: When ready: +2/+2 for good on a random friendly creature, maybe itself (a graft); side effect: it loses 2 Health for good.
cards.picture: A lion with a goat's head sprouting from its back and a snake for a tail, all three wearing hospital ID wristbands, in a lab enclosure with a sticky note: DO NOT FEED AFTER MIDNIGHT.

cards.name: Resurrected T-Rex
cards.flavor: Sixty-six million years asleep. Woke up hungry.
cards.notes: A huge abomination, On the Brink. Side effect: its cloned DNA is unstable, it loses 1 Health for good each Dusk, until it hits twice as hard.
cards.picture: A T-Rex skeleton half covered in new flesh breaking out of a museum display, the DNA sequencer that brought it back still beeping, a guide pointing at the exit.

cards.name: Longevity Hub
cards.flavor: Live forever. Subscription renews monthly.
cards.notes: Utopia's healer (its primary mechanic): each Dawn every other friendly creature heals 2. Pairs with Brink creatures that hurt themselves.
cards.picture: A gleaming white clinic in the desert where billionaires lie in pods drinking smoothies through tubes, a young intern on a treadmill in the corner wired to them by a blood line.

cards.name: Femtosecond Laser
cards.flavor: Faster than a thought. Cleaner than a scalpel.
cards.notes: Clean removal for Utopia: 4 damage to target creature or player, with no cost to you (Black Hole and Splitting The Atom both hurt you).
cards.picture: A laser beam the thickness of a hair slicing a falling apple into perfect quarters in mid-air, a physicist in safety goggles timing it with a stopwatch.

cards.name: Quark
cards.flavor: Up, down, charm, strange. Mostly strange.
cards.notes: A leaper that grows: Leapfrog, and Grow 1 (+1/+1 each Dawn, for good: persistent growth, Utopia's primary). Cheap, ready at once.
cards.picture: Three tiny glowing particles in colored hats bouncing on a trampoline inside an atom, one of them flipping off the edge with a grin.

cards.name: Seasteading
cards.flavor: No taxes. No laws. No lifeboats.
cards.notes: Armor 3 on every friendly creature (Armor wins 65% in the study; Utopia's primary). A libertarian floating city.
cards.picture: A floating hexagonal platform city in the middle of the ocean, tech-bros sunbathing on the deck while one corner quietly sinks and a lone lifeguard chair stands empty.

cards.name: Ankylorhiza
cards.flavor: Twenty-five million years extinct. Still holds a grudge.
cards.notes: A big body for a faction whose bodies burn out: Arrival: Armor 3 on itself. An extinct toothed whale, de-extinct.
cards.picture: A huge prehistoric whale with a crocodile's teeth bursting out of a lab aquarium tank, water and glass everywhere, a scientist in a lab coat clutching a sign reading DE-EXTINCTION: PHASE 1.

cards.name: White Dwarf
cards.flavor: Small. Very white. Incredibly dense.
cards.notes: A dense wall: Unbothered (enemy effects can't lower its stats; the study's best ability, 65%). Ready at once.
cards.picture: A dwarf like those of The Lord of the Rings standing in space, glowing white like the star: a long braided beard, a winged helm, a double-bladed axe, chain mail, the planets around him bending toward him, unbothered.

cards.name: Biohacker
cards.flavor: Microdoses, cold plunges, and a chip in his hand that opens the fridge.
cards.notes: Hormesis (Poison Heal): Burn heals it instead of hurting it. Its Arrival gives it Burn 2 for 3 Days, so it heals 2 each Dusk. Utopia's self-harm becomes fuel.
cards.picture: A shirtless tech bro in an ice bath full of glowing green sludge, sensors taped all over his chest, his smartwatch showing 'biological age: 19'.

cards.name: Prion Disease
cards.flavor: Misfolded, contagious, and in no hurry.
cards.notes: Burn 3 for 3 Days on target creature: 9 damage in all. Slow removal.
cards.picture: A cow in a lab coat staring blankly into a microscope while its own brain, full of holes like Swiss cheese, floats in a jar beside it.

cards.name: Heimlich Maneuver
cards.flavor: Science saves lives. Ribs, less so.
cards.notes: Logistics Maneuver: push target friendly creature a step back (the Vanguard to a Flank, a Flank to its Headquarters slot); a creature already there trades places with it. Gets a hurt one out of the front line.
cards.picture: A scientist in a lab coat performing the Heimlich maneuver on a robot, a glowing chip flying out of its mouth across the lab while a colleague times it on a clipboard.
